research_updates.notes: Sources checked: SEC Exhibits 21 for 2021-2025, Utah PSC dockets 20-035-04 and 24-035-04, Utah DEQ source N159410007, Meta's Eagle Mountain pages, IM3 building inventory, Utah County land records, and Eagle Mountain city records for 2018-2026. Queries used Meta, Facebook, Stadion LLC, Eagle Mountain Data Center, EAG1-EAG7, UCO, 1499 North Pony Express Parkway, 1275 North Community Circle, and the original parcel numbers 59:057:0003/0004. Stadion is a Meta subsidiary and the operator record resolves to the campus, but no public crosswalk maps IM3 building 01024051963 to an EAG identifier; all campus values remain unallocated. No public-record requests were made.

research_updates.title: Operator and regulatory disclosures — later actual anchors replace two opening forecasts
research_updates.notes: Sources checked: Meta opening releases, current and cached factsheets, Meta annual sustainability materials, SEC 10-Ks and subsidiary exhibits, Utah PSC Stadion testimony and exhibits from 2020-2026, and Eagle Mountain ACFR/APFR principal-employer tables for 2021-2024. Queries used Eagle Mountain investment, capex, operations jobs, employee, FTE, payroll, wage, revenue, expense, special contract, reserved capacity, demand and load. The 2024 sworn filing supports cumulative investment above $1.5 billion and more than 300 operations jobs, while city ACFR statistical tables add an annual Stadion headcount series of 66, 66, 96 and 96 for fiscal years 2021-2024. Those employee snapshots are not additive to the broader jobs-supported figure and do not identify FTE status, payroll, worker residence, contractor inclusion or building allocation. The 2021 more-than-$1-billion and more-than-200-job values remain correctly labeled source forecasts. No annual capex, depreciation, campus revenue, operating expense, payroll, wage or selected-building allocation was found.

source.title: Redacted Direct Testimony of Kyra Coyle on Behalf of Stadion LLC, Utah PSC Docket 24-035-04
source.notes: Sworn utility-rate testimony filed for Stadion, a Meta subsidiary and Rocky Mountain Power special-contract customer. Printed page 6 reports more than $1.5 billion invested in Utah and more than 300 operations jobs; the public copy redacts facility load and does not disclose payroll, annual capital spending, electricity use, or customer payments.

research_updates.title: Construction and permit audit — equipment counts retained without converting permits to spend
research_updates.notes: Sources checked: Utah DAQ permits N159410005, N159410007 and the 2026 N159410011 status entry; Eagle Mountain building and planning portals; Utah public-meeting packets; Meta construction releases; ENR coverage; and address/building-ID searches from 2018-2026. The December 2022 record lists 29 existing generators and fourteen proposed units for two buildings, preserved with separate bases. Meta's 2021 opening release reports a 1,250-worker historical peak while a later factsheet says 1,200; the baseline 1,250 observation is retained and the conflict documented rather than averaged. No permit valuation, contract total, completion invoice, worker hours, residence, payroll, or building-specific construction expenditure was found.

source.title: Intent to Approve DAQE-IN159410007-22, Stadion Eagle Mountain Data Center
source.notes: The permit record identifies Stadion at 1499 North Pony Express Parkway, five existing EAG buildings, 29 existing diesel emergency generators, and a proposal for fourteen additional generators serving two UCO buildings. It is an intent-to-approve document rather than evidence that the proposed generators were finally authorized or commissioned; potential emissions and maximum testing hours are not actual use.

research_updates.title: Supplier audit — firms are identifiable but local spending is not
research_updates.notes: Sources checked: ENR/AGC coverage, Mortenson project and safety coverage, city permit and infrastructure materials, Meta partner pages, procurement/vendor searches, and named-company searches for 2018-2026. ENR identifies Mortenson as builder and Forterra Structural Precast's Utah offices as an insulated-panel supplier; the infrastructure agreement also mentions Psomas review and inspection staffing. No source reports contract values, invoices, supplier payments, Utah County establishment addresses, worker residence, procurement totals, or a locally retained purchasing share. The supplier channel therefore remains missing rather than being inferred from firm names.

source.title: AGC of Utah Contractors Look Forward to More Growth in 2019
source.notes: Construction trade coverage identifies Minneapolis-based Mortenson as builder and Forterra Structural Precast's Utah offices as supplying insulated precast panels. It reports no contract values, invoice amounts, worker residence, payroll, or Utah County share and therefore cannot support a supplier-spending observation.

research_updates.title: Electric utility audit — supporting capacity is not facility consumption
research_updates.notes: Sources checked: Rocky Mountain Power Schedule 34 releases and Utah tariffs; PSC dockets 20-035-04, 24-035-04 and large-load line-extension materials; Meta renewable-energy reports and factsheets; EIA facility and utility datasets; and searches for Stadion meter, kWh, MWh, MW, peak demand, bill and rate from 2018-2026. The current operator factsheet describes thirteen Utah projects adding 1,719 MW, retained only as an unallocated source projection. The PSC filing confirms special-contract service but redacts facility load. No actual campus kWh, billed demand, annual electricity payment, PUE, renewable generation delivered, or selected-building meter was public.

research_updates.title: Water and wastewater audit — reuse benefit is measurable, campus withdrawal is not
research_updates.notes: Sources checked: Eagle Mountain's 2018 Stadion water/sewer agreement index, 2022 infrastructure agreement, 2024 reuse article and conservation plan, Meta 2023-2024 water-benefit reports, Utah Division of Water Rights listings and mail logs, and Division of Water Quality materials. Queries covered Stadion, Facebook, Meta, 1499 Pony Express, cooling water, wastewater, reuse, withdrawal, consumption, acre-feet, gallons and water rights from 2018-2026. The city reports 77,715,648 gallons of potable irrigation displacement in 2024 and Meta reports watershed-restoration benefits, but neither is facility use. Water-right records 54-459/54-1470 name Eagle Mountain Data Center Campus LLC, not Stadion/Meta, and were excluded as a separate developer. No Meta meter, annual withdrawal, consumptive use, sewer volume, rate or payment was found.

source.title: Eagle Mountain City Water Conservation and Management Plan
source.notes: The adopted plan reports that the first reuse line and booster station were operating for the 2024 irrigation season and displaced 77,715,648 gallons of potable irrigation water. That avoided municipal withdrawal is not Meta facility consumption, a water right, a utility payment, or an annual project operating-cost measure.

research_updates.title: Fiscal and assessor audit — two taxpayer-value years observed, tax cash flows still absent
research_updates.notes: Sources checked: Utah County 2022 and 2023 ACFRs and the 2025 budget statistical tables, county land-record abstracts and property-search entry points, Alpine School District budgets, original and current parcel searches, and owner-name searches for Stadion LLC and Meta from 2018-2026. Utah County reports Stadion taxable assessed value of $242.682 million in 2022 and $305.404 million in 2023, retained as a same-scope annual series. An Alpine School District table reports $358.043091 million under its own principal-taxpayer presentation; its basis cannot be reconciled with the county table, so it is not mixed into the series. No parcel/account roll tying the full value to the campus, property-tax bill, payment, recipient distribution, exemption amount, personal-property split, or 2024-2026 same-scope value was found.

source.title: Utah County Annual Comprehensive Financial Report 2023
source.notes: The statistical section's principal-property-taxpayer table is sourced to the Utah County Treasurer and reports values in thousands. Stadion LLC is ranked fifth for 2023 at $305.404 million, or 0.35 percent of total county taxable assessed value; the table is not a tax bill, cash receipt, parcel roll, or campus-only valuation.

research_updates.title: Incentive and public-cost audit — contingent terms do not establish realized subsidy
research_updates.notes: Sources checked: Sweetwater Industrial Park CRA #1 plan, budget, participation agreement, and interlocal amendments; 2018 approved minutes; city budgets and amendments for FY2019-FY2024; city ACFRs; Transparent Utah vendor-payment and transaction entry points; county and school materials; and exact searches for Stadion/Meta reimbursement, tax increment, PILOT, grant, incentive, disbursement and service cost through 2026. Agreements specify participation percentages, 20-year phase periods, a 40-year outside limit, and entity-specific real-property caps while personal-property reimbursement remains formula-driven. The March 19, 2024 worksheet proposed $3.288 million in budget authority for 'Energy Tax Reimbursement - Meta Development Agreement,' but June 18 minutes expressly describe the reimbursement increase as a placeholder whose actual expenditure depends on funds received. Aggregate RDA reimbursement-agreement expenditures and Sweetwater tax-increment receipts are not split to Stadion in the reviewed public statements. No realized Stadion reimbursement ledger, same-scope service-cost series, or fiscal net was found. The roughly $5 million city-built reuse project is a bounded gross project cost with unresolved funding, not the complete public cost of the campus.

research_updates.title: Land, infrastructure, bond and court audit — obligations found, cash evidence absent
research_updates.notes: Sources checked: original county parcels 59:057:0003/0004 and subdivision abstracts, 2018 development and water/sewer agreement indexes, the 2022 Master Infrastructure Agreement and orders, Eagle Mountain budgets and capital materials, Utah Treasurer/Finance Commission bond materials, Utah court/public-index searches, SEC filings, and exact Stadion/entity/address searches for 2018-2026. The agreement allocates construction or reimbursement duties for off-site infrastructure but contains no completed payment schedule; a $1.8 million Pony Express resurfacing item is expressly associated with Google reimbursement and was excluded. No project bond, mortgage amount, litigation recovery, mechanics-lien total, deed consideration, completed public advance, or Stadion reimbursement amount was found.

research_updates.title: Expansion audit — later phases are not silently folded into the selected project
research_updates.notes: Sources checked: city and Utah public-notice records for Sweetwater CRA areas #1-#4, Stadion South Expansion, 2025 development agreements, 2026 notices, parcel-owner tables, DEQ N159410011, and contemporary operator/trade reporting. The original operating campus, later UCO buildings, the southern expansion and other Eagle Mountain data-center projects occupy distinct records and sometimes distinct parcels. New QTS, Google, Tract, Williams and Sweetwater #2/#4 values were excluded unless a source explicitly tied them to the original Meta operating campus. The project account therefore does not treat all Stadion-owned land or every later agreement as one realized facility.

research_updates.title: Community audit — cumulative and named-recipient amounts are kept overlap-aware
research_updates.notes: Sources checked: Meta factsheets and opening release, Community Action Grant recipient pages for 2019-2026, Eagle Mountain city announcements and council minutes, Alpine School District and Utah nonprofit pages, and searches for grant, donation, sponsorship, school, nonprofit, volunteer and recipient amounts. The current factsheet reports more than $5.2 million to Utah County schools and nonprofits and 280-plus grants/sponsorships; city sources independently identify a $250,000 Launch Pad grant and a $121,000 Meta grant to the University of Utah for the observatory park project. Both named amounts are nested within the cumulative program and are retained with explicit anti-summation notes. The 2025 city recipient roster reports more than $1 million across 109 Utah County projects but no recipient amounts and is lower than the current cumulative total, so it adds no separate measurement. No full annual ledger, in-kind valuation, recipient reconciliation, volunteer-hour value, or causal community outcome was found.

research_updates.title: Journalism and trade-press audit — corroboration retained as search evidence, not preferred measurements
research_updates.notes: Sources checked: KSL/Deseret News, FOX13, Engineering News-Record, Data Center Dynamics/indexed trade coverage, contractor pages and local reporting from announcement through September 2026. Queries combined Meta/Facebook/Stadion with Eagle Mountain, construction, opening, expansion, contractor, supplier, jobs, tax, power and water. Reporting corroborates the July 2021 opening and identifies contractors, but repeats operator estimates or conflicts on campus floor area (about 1.5 million versus Meta's nearly 2.4 million square feet). No unique, better-supported payment, employment, payroll, utility-use, tax, supplier-spend or public-cost observation survived preference for primary records.

research_updates.title: Last-resort contribution-model decision table — no eligible synthesis retained
research_updates.notes: Candidate-by-candidate gate after direct-source exhaustion: (1) selected-building investment by 344,790-square-foot area share of campus capex — REJECTED because no IM3-to-EAG crosswalk exists, reported campus floor areas conflict, equipment intensity is nonuniform, and cumulative spending has no phase denominator; (2) construction job-years or labor income from the 1,250-worker peak — REJECTED because peak workers are not hours, duration, residence, payroll or construction-only spending; (3) construction output and indirect/induced effects from the greater-than-$1.5-billion campus investment — REJECTED because the total is cumulative campus investment rather than dated construction expenditure and no sourced local-purchase share or applicable input-output coefficients were found; (4) supplier/local spending from Mortenson, Forterra and Psomas names — REJECTED because no contracts, invoices, establishment-level vendor geography, payment dates or locally retained share were public; (5) direct operating payroll from the 2021-2024 Stadion employee series times a wage benchmark — REJECTED because the headcounts are not defined as FTE, occupation mix, wages, benefits, worker residence or selected-building staff; (6) operating indirect/induced contribution from the more-than-300 jobs-supported claim — REJECTED because that total already has undisclosed direct/contractor/induced composition and no direct operating expenditure or nonoverlapping multiplier base exists; (7) property tax from assessed value times a tax rate — REJECTED because the company-county values do not identify real versus personal property, parcel/tax-area mix, exemptions, bills, collections, recipient shares or CRA diversion; (8) realized municipal-energy-tax reimbursement from the $3.288-million FY2024 appropriation — REJECTED because the city later calls the budget a placeholder, and no Stadion request, eligible MET payment, city collection or disbursement record is public; (9) realized tax-increment reimbursement from Sweetwater receipts or aggregate RDA reimbursement expenditures — REJECTED because neither series is split to Stadion and mixing project-area receipts with all-agreement expenses would violate same-scope reconciliation; (10) net fiscal contribution — REJECTED because taxes paid, incentive disbursements, recurring service costs and supporting-infrastructure funding are not available for the same government, period and scope; (11) electricity use or payments from renewable nameplate MW, 1,000-MW regional delivery capacity, generator counts or assumed load factor/PUE — REJECTED because campus load and bills are redacted, statewide generation is nonexclusive, and no meter, PUE or operating-hour observations exist; (12) water use, cost or net benefit from 77,715,648 gallons of park irrigation displacement or Meta restoration volumes — REJECTED because these are off-site avoided municipal withdrawal or modeled watershed benefits, not campus withdrawal, consumption, sewer flow, rate or payment; (13) annual or per-recipient community benefit by dividing the greater-than-$5.2-million cumulative total — REJECTED because the period start, annual amounts, recipient ledger, in-kind valuation and outcomes are undisclosed and the $250,000 and $121,000 grants overlap the total. Result: suppliers and complete public costs remain explicitly missing; no candidate meets the policy's input, geographic, temporal, nonoverlap and decision-relevance gates.

research_updates.title: Government-statistics and county-outcome audit — no defensible comparison model retained
research_updates.notes: Sources checked: the governed 2001-2024 county economic panel, BEA CAEMP25N/CAINC/real-GDP regional files, BLS QCEW county employment and wage files, Census County Business Patterns, county peers in Utah and neighboring states, and Utah economic-development context. Queries covered Utah County real GDP, employment, average weekly wage, NAICS 518/51, establishment counts, data-center opening, comparator counties, pre-trend, synthetic control and difference-in-differences. Utah County has rapid population growth, semiconductor and technology investment, multiple data-center projects, and no source-registered untreated comparison group or clean campus-only treatment date; the July 2021 opening overlaps construction continuing after operation began and later phases. The public county panels are useful context but do not isolate the selected building or Stadion.

research_updates.title: County-outcome model candidate decision table — GDP, employment and wage candidates rejected separately
research_updates.notes: Dedicated metric-level gate: GDP candidate A, Utah County pre/post trend break around July 2021 — REJECTED because 2018 construction, 2021 partial operation, continued construction and later expansions create no single treatment date, and concurrent population, semiconductor and other data-center growth dominate the county series. GDP candidate B, matched-county difference-in-differences or synthetic control — REJECTED because no defensible donor pool survives the required comparable pre-trend, growth, industry mix and absence-of-data-center-treatment checks; ad hoc weights would be analyst-selected rather than source-registered. GDP candidate C, allocate campus investment to county GDP with an input-output multiplier — REJECTED because cumulative campus investment is not annual local final demand, local purchase shares and coefficients are missing, and construction output would overlap any observed county GDP change. Employment candidate A, before/after county total-employment change — REJECTED because county employment combines all industries and demographic growth and cannot separate the 66-96 observed Stadion employees from unrelated changes. Employment candidate B, county matched comparison or synthetic control — REJECTED because treatment timing and donor validity fail as for GDP, while QCEW suppression and classification prevent a clean data-center industry series. Employment candidate C, scale the Stadion annual headcount to county effects with an employment multiplier — REJECTED because no sourced local direct/indirect split, contractor inclusion, worker residence, payroll base or applicable multiplier exists, and the greater-than-300 jobs-supported figure may already include multiplier channels. Wage candidate A, pre/post QCEW average-weekly-wage gap — REJECTED because the aggregate is composition-sensitive and no Stadion wage or occupational mix is public. Wage candidate B, matched-county wage difference-in-differences — REJECTED because the donor/pre-trend and treatment-timing failures remain and semiconductor/technology composition shifts are concurrent. Wage candidate C, impute payroll or wage uplift from industry averages — REJECTED because headcounts are not FTE, NAICS assignment is not established, occupations and benefits are unknown, and an imputed payroll cannot identify a county-wide wage effect. Result: study.modeled_county_gdp_comparison_gap, study.modeled_county_employment_comparison_gap and study.modeled_county_wage_comparison_gap remain missing with distinct failed eligibility conditions rather than a blanket rejection.

research_updates.title: Contribution-account disposition — direct anchors improved, unsupported channels remain open
research_updates.notes: After deduplication, direct observations cover construction, investment, operations, fiscal, resources and community. This corrective pass adds four annual Stadion employee snapshots, a second county assessed-value year and a second named community grant; all remain campus/company-county observations unallocated to the selected IM3 footprint. Supplier spending remains unobserved. Public-cost evidence is limited to a roughly $5 million city-built reuse project with unresolved funding plus Meta reimbursement budget authority expressly described as a placeholder, so neither satisfies the full public-cost category or supports net-fiscal synthesis. Facility electricity and water use, FTE/payroll, annual capex, tax payments, realized incentive reimbursements and all three county comparison modules remain unresolved. Thirteen contribution candidates and nine metric-specific county candidates were tested and rejected for stated input, scope, timing, overlap or comparator failures; zero modeled records were added.
